editorial:
Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe is a Universal Pictures sound serial directed by Ford Beebe and Ray Taylor. The Internet Archive holds Part 1, a 19-minute black-and-white episode. Its description has Flash, Dale and Zarkov returning to Planet Mongo to find an antidote for the Purple Death. A creator would want it as ready-made period science-fiction adventure footage.

The rights question is unresolved. The Archive dates the item 1941 and the queue says 1940. Either way it was published after 1930, so its print is free only if its copyright was not renewed in the 28th-year window. I could not confirm a renewal or its absence, and the Archive item gives no license. Check the renewal records before reusing the footage. The Flash Gordon characters and source material carry their own rights, and the film's copyright expiring would not end them.
faq: Is Flash Gordon Conquers the Universe public domain?

Not established. It is a Universal serial from 1940 or 1941 (sources differ), so it is free only if its copyright was never renewed. I could not confirm that either way, and the Internet Archive item specifies no license.
Can I use the Flash Gordon characters in a new work?
Not safely. The film's copyright status does not settle any separate rights in the characters or source material. I did not confirm those rights, so clear them independently.
